title: Notations
body_md:
We use normal-face letters for scalars, boldface lower-case letters for vectors, boldface upper-case letters for matrices, and italic boldface upper-case letters for random vectors.
For $N\in\mathbb{N}_+$, $[N]$ denotes the set $\{1, 2, \dots, N\}$.
The clipping function is denoted by $\operatorname{clip}_B(x)=\min(B, \max(-B, x))$.
We use $(z)_+$ and $(z)_-$ to denote $\max(z, 0)$ and $\min(z, 0)$, respectively.
We use $\operatorname{KL}(\cdot\|\cdot)$ to denote the KL-divergence, $D_{\mathrm{H}}(\cdot, \cdot)$ to denote the Hellinger distance, and $\chi^2(\cdot\|\cdot)$ to denote the $\chi^2$-distance.

title: Setup
body_md:
All samplers reveal blocks of a uniform size, taken as consecutive chunks of a uniformly random permutation of $[L]$ drawn independently of the tokens.
We run SIRS{}-RB with block size $n$ and $B\in\{\tfrac18, \tfrac14, \tfrac12, 1, 2\}$, and compare it with parallel sampling with block size $n'$ and with sequential decoding ($n'=1$), which is exact.
For each sampler we compute the KL-divergence $\operatorname{KL}(p^*\|\widehat p_B)$ from the data distribution to the output distribution, in nats per sequence and averaged over permutations, and the expected number of score queries per sequence. Parallel sampling uses $\lceil L/n'\rceil$ queries; in SIRS{}-RB we flip the coins of the Poissonized Bernoulli factory one at a time and reject at the first failure, which leaves the output distribution unchanged and saves queries.
